I feel with quality signings in defence and midfield, they could mount a decent challenge for the Premier League next season. How do you feel they will fare? – Sterling.There’s an odd sense that Michael Carrick’s level of achievement last season was at precisely the most awkward level for the board. United didn’t produce indisputably brilliant football under him but equally 12 wins and three draws in 17 games was good enough that they pretty much had to give him the job. But it’s one thing to turn out those kinds of results when the pressure’s off, you’re already out of both cup competitions and you don’t have any European football; it’s quite another to do it in the heat of a full season. items.title: Julian Alvarez and Diego Simeone reportedly set for face-to-face meeting to define his future amid Barcelona’s final offer
items.description:
With FC Barcelona still looking for the striker's signing with a final offer, Julian Alvarez and Diego Simeone are reportedly set to have a face-to-face meeting to define his future at Atletico Madrid. 
Julian Alvarez‘s future has evolved into one of the marquee storylines of the 2026 summer transfer window following the striker’s public admission of his desire to depart Atletico Madrid. With FC Barcelona still actively pursuing his signature, Alvarez and head coach Diego “Cholo” Simeone are reportedly scheduled to hold a crucial face-to-face meeting to resolve the forward’s status.



Simeone has maintained a clear public stance, aligning with club leadership’s decision to retain Alvarez as a foundational piece for Atletico’s 2026-27 campaign. Following his participation in the 2026 World Cup, where he reiterated his intent to seek an exit to pursue a new challenge, Alvarez will return from vacation on Monday, August10, when the pivotal sit-down will take place.



According to TyC Sports journalist and Argentina insider Gaston Edul, Julian Alvarez and Simeone will meet face-to-face on Monday to directly address the player’s future. However, the positions held by both parties remain firmly entrenched.



Per Edul, after consulting those in the striker’s inner circle, Alvarez considers his tenure at Atletico to be complete and no longer wishes to remain with the club. Conversely, Atletico executives maintain an unyielding position, refusing to negotiate a departure unless an interested club triggers his €500 million (roughly $578 million USD) release clause.



Atletico Madrid coach Diego Simeone interacts with Julian Alvarez after being subbed off. (Aitor Alcalde/Getty Images)



Simeone will attempt to persuade Alvarez to remain at the Metropolitano and commit to the club’s long-term vision. On the other hand, the forward aims to de-escalate tensions, which grew uncomfortable for him following the media reaction generated by the club’s public social media responses during the World Cup.


        


With triggering the full release clause ruled out by all suitors, Barcelona‘s reported strategy is to present a formal offer worth €120 million (roughly $138 million USD), which would represent the highest proposal submitted for the Argentine star. Whether Atletico considers the bid will depend heavily on the outcome of the discussions between player and coach, mirroring the process when Alvarez met with Pep Guardiola to facilitate his exit from Manchester City.



Barcelona remains preferred destination despite Arsenal and PSG interest



Alvarez has drawn interest not only from Barcelona, his preferred destination, but also from Arsenal and Paris Saint-Germain, two clubs capable of financing a transfer of this magnitude. Nevertheless, the Blaugrana remains the top choice for the Argentine international.



According to Edul, even though Arsenal and PSG have submitted formal inquiries, moving outside of Spain remains a secondary option for the player. Alvarez chose to depart Manchester primarily for family reasons, making a return to England, more specific to London, an undesirable outcome for his personal situation.

items.title: PSG ready to add Japanese goalkeeper Zion Suzuki, but immediate role remains uncertain
items.description:
Paris Saint-Germain are in the final stages of closing a deal with Parma for star Japanese goalkeeper Zion Suzuki, though his immediate role with the club remains uncertain. 
The 2026 FIFA World Cup prompted many moves in soccer. Now, Paris Saint-Germain have decided to go for a star of the competition, closing in on a deal with Parma for goalkeeper Zion Suzuki.



As reported by Fabrizio Romano, PSG and Parma are set to seal a deal where Japanese goalkeeper Zion Suzuki would join the French side for around $40 million (€35 million).



However, Suzuki’s role with PSG is yet to be determined. It will all depend on Lucas Chevalier, who has rotated starts with Matvey Safonov. Chevalier is rumored to leave, and if he does, Suzuki would fight for the starting role against the Russian keeper.



A ripple effect at PSG



Chevalier, 24, is currently followed by Juventus. The Italian side see it as a top priority to bring in a new goalkeeper—specifically a young yet experienced shot-stopper who has already played in a top European league.



If Chevalier stays, the alternative move involves Zion Suzuki. PSG reached an agreement for Parma’s goalkeeper to give Juventus options where the French club still secure a strategic advantage.


        


Under this scenario, Suzuki could remain in Italy to play for Juventus on loan from PSG. The Ligue 1 side still have to determine whether Chevalier stays to fight for the starting spot or if Suzuki is the better option to compete with Safonov.

items.title: Why isn’t Lionel Messi playing for Inter Miami vs Monterrey in 2026 Leagues Cup?
items.description:
The Argentine superstar had only just returned to the starting lineup and delivered a spectacular performance in the opening match, but unfortunate circumstances have now forced him away from the team. 
Lionel Messi will be missing when Inter Miami faces Monterrey in a crucial 2026 Leagues Cup clash, leaving the club without its biggest attacking weapon at a particularly important moment in the tournament. The Argentine superstar had only just returned to the starting lineup and delivered a spectacular performance in the opening match, but unfortunate circumstances have now forced him away from the team.



The absence immediately changes the complexion of the matchup, especially with Inter Miami already dealing with several other attacking problems. Monterrey, meanwhile, enters the contest knowing that a victory could dramatically improve its chances of staying alive in the competition after losing its opening match to Orlando City.



Messi’s absence comes only days after one of his most impressive performances of the summer. The 39-year-old started Inter Miami’s Leagues Cup opener against Atlético de San Luis and scored twice while also providing an assist in a 4-2 victory, directly contributing to three of the club’s four goals.



It was the Argentine’s first start for Inter Miami since returning from the 2026 World Cup with La Albiceleste, and his performance immediately reminded everyone why the club remains so dependent on him. He looked sharp throughout the match, constantly finding space between the lines and creating problems whenever he received the ball around the penalty area.









The result also gave the Herons an important early advantage in the revamped Leagues Cup format. With only three Phase One matches available and goal difference playing a major role in determining who advances, every goal can become valuable later in the competition. However, Messi will now have to watch from afar as Inter Miami takes on one of the strongest clubs from Liga MX.



Why isn’t Lionel Messi playing against Monterrey?



The reason behind Messi’s absence is deeply personal and far more significant than a routine injury, suspension or decision to rotate the squad. Jorge Messi, Lionel Messi’s father and longtime agent, died in Rosario at the age of 68, with his death confirmed on Saturday after he had been receiving medical treatment. The news has prompted tributes from various organizations and clubs, including the Argentine Football Association (AFA) and Barcelona.



Our deepest condolences. May Jorge Messi rest in peace. pic.twitter.com/PPSTTjHki1— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) August 8, 2026 



Messi has subsequently traveled to Argentina to be with his family during this extremely difficult period. Reports indicate that he is expected to reunite with his mother Celia Cuccittini, his siblings and other relatives in Rosario, where arrangements for a private ceremony are expected to take place.



Sending our deepest strength to Leo Messi and his family.We’re with you during this difficult time and sending you our warmest embrace. pic.twitter.com/YOCenOHSWy— Selección Argentina in English (@AFASeleccionEN) August 8, 2026 



The decision to leave Inter Miami at this moment is therefore completely understandable. Soccer has understandably taken a back seat as Messi returns home to mourn his father and support his family.



Painful moment overshadows a crucial match



There is an important soccer story developing around the Inter Miami-Monterrey meeting, but Messi’s absence puts everything else into perspective. The Leagues Cup remains important, particularly with both clubs fighting for a place in the knockout rounds, yet the circumstances surrounding the Argentine’s departure understandably dominate the conversation.



Miami enters the match with three points after its opening victory, while Monterrey has no points after its defeat to Orlando City. The Mexican club needs a result, while Inter Miami wants to strengthen its position before its final Phase One fixture against Club Leon.







The 39-year-old absence is made even more significant by the number of other attacking players unavailable to Inter Miami. Luis Suarez is suspended for the Leagues Cup, while Tadeo Allende, German Berterame and Mateo Silvetti have also been dealing with injury issues.



That leaves Inter Miami with an unusually depleted forward line against a Monterrey side that desperately needs a result. The club’s attacking responsibilities are therefore likely to fall on players who normally operate in different roles.

items.title: The role Jorge Messi played behind the scenes in Lionel’s historic career
items.description:
Jorge Messi was far more than a father to Lionel — from his first coach to his lifelong agent, he shaped nearly every step of his son's historic career. 
Jorge Messi, who passed away Friday at the age of 68 after a long illness, was far more than a father figure in Lionel Messi‘s career — he was its architect, working almost entirely behind the scenes for over two decades to shape one of football’s greatest stories.



His role began long before the world took notice. Jorge served as Lionel’s first coach at Grandoli, a neighborhood club in Rosario, when his son was just four years old, laying the groundwork for the talent that would later catch the eye of Newell’s Old Boys.



He remained a constant presence through Lionel’s diagnosis with growth hormone deficiency, standing by him through an expensive and complicated treatment process the family struggled to afford.



It was Jorge who then made what’s often described as one of football’s riskiest decisions: uprooting the family to relocate to Barcelona, leaving behind stable work in Argentina. That gamble led directly to the club’s famous napkin agreement with Carles Rexach in December 2000, which secured both Lionel’s signing and the funding for his ongoing medical treatment.



Lionel Messi with his father Jorge at Barcelona. (Imago)



As Lionel’s career took off, Jorge’s role evolved from guardian into full-time representative. He left his job at the steel factory to become his son’s sole agent for the next 22 years, negotiating every major contract renewal at Barcelona, orchestrating the move to PSG, and closing the historic arrival at Inter Miami.


        


Messi’s lifelong reliance on his father’s approval



In an interview with Luzu TV earlier this year, Messi opened up about just how much he relied on his father’s perspective throughout his career, offering a rare glimpse into the emotional weight behind Jorge’s role in his journey.



“On the sporting side, I was always my own harshest critic — I know when I did things well and when I did them badly. But I always needed my old man’s approval or opinion, ever since I was little. I’d finish a match and ask him about anything,” he said.

items.description: Brazilian excels at winning free-kicks and conjuring results from them, hence why the champions were willing to spend £75mBruno Guimarães has broken a very niche record. His £75m move to Arsenal is the most expensive transfer for a midfielder aged at least 28. This should not be taken too seriously given the previous record holder, Zinedine Zidane, moved 25 years ago from Juventus to Real Madrid, and would have cost far more in 2026 money. But it shows how highly the Gunners rate the Brazilian to have spent so much on a player who will be in his 30s before the end of next year. It is a transfer for today, not tomorrow.The question is why. One reason is that Guimarães rarely misses matches. Another is that he can play anywhere across midfield in the 4-3-3 formation Mikel Arteta often deploys. These attributes could be priceless with Declan Rice managing long-term nerve pain in his hamstring and Martin Ødegaard playing 40% of possible Premier League minutes last season. items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al-Nassr finally clears major $280 million hurdle as Samu Costa move edges closer
items.description:
The breakthrough could have an immediate impact on the squad, with Costa's move from Mallorca now edging significantly closer to completion. 
Al-Nassr has reportedly cleared the obstacle that previously hindered its summer transfer plans, paving the way for immediate squad improvements. This significant breakthrough brings Samu Costa’s highly anticipated transfer from Mallorca to join Cristiano Ronaldo significantly closer to completion.



The timing could hardly be more important for Al-Nassr. The club is preparing for the start of a new campaign in which it will be expected to defend its Saudi league crown while also challenging for the AFC Champions League Elite, and strengthening the midfield has been one of its priorities.



For several weeks, however, the club’s recruitment plans had been complicated by circumstances away from the pitch. An agreement for Costa had reportedly been reached in July, but the Saudi side was unable to formally complete the transfer while it worked through a regulatory process connected to its finances.



Al-Nassr finally clears the path for new signings



According to Saudi newspaper Al-Riyadiyah, Al-Nassr has completed the procedures required to end the financial monitoring imposed on the club, allowing it to move forward with registering new players and completing transfers for the upcoming season.



The report indicates that the club has submitted the necessary documentation to the relevant authorities as it works toward formally lifting the remaining restrictions. That development represents a major breakthrough for Al-Nassr, which had effectively been prevented from turning previously agreed transfer deals into official registrations.



New kit. Same hunger. pic.twitter.com/Tdg94bBOBF— Al Nassr Zone (@TheNassrZone) July 30, 2026



The process has reportedly involved the Public Investment Fund (PIF), the Al-Nassr Club Company and the restructuring of existing financial commitments. New commercial agreements with HUMAIN and Aroya Cruise Saudi have also reportedly formed part of the measures used to strengthen the club’s financial position.



Specialized consulting firms were brought in to help Al-Nassr improve its financial, administrative, legal and commercial operations. The broader aim has been to establish tighter spending controls and create a more sustainable structure for the club moving forward.



The $280 million hurdle finally comes into focus



The scale of the problem becomes clearer when looking at the figures involved. Al-Nassr accumulated liabilities exceeding 800 million Saudi riyals, with estimates placing the overall burden at around $280 million, creating serious complications for the club’s ability to operate freely in the transfer market.



Reports cited by various outlets linked the financial pressure to years of aggressive spending, major player salaries and expensive recruitment. Cristiano Ronaldo’s enormous contract has inevitably been part of the discussion, although it would be unfair to attribute the club’s entire financial situation to the Portuguese superstar.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr lifts the Saudi Pro League Trophy



Ronaldo joined Al-Nassr in 2023 after leaving Manchester United, and his arrival transformed the Saudi football landscape. His presence helped attract other global stars to the league and gave Al-Nassr unprecedented worldwide visibility, but his reported earnings have also made the club’s wage bill considerably heavier.



Reports have claimed that the superstar has earned around $625 million in wages during his time at Al-Nassr, although figures surrounding player contracts and commercial arrangements can vary between sources. The club has also invested heavily in other high-profile players, adding further pressure to its finances.



The Saudi club’s situation eventually led to intervention from the Public Investment Fund (PIF), which placed greater scrutiny on its financial operations and restricted spending that lacked sufficient backing. The restructuring process has now apparently reached a stage where Al-Nassr can return to the transfer market with fewer restrictions.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr celebrates with the Saudi Pro League Trophy.



Samu Costa move can finally move forward



That breakthrough directly affects the future of Samu Costa, who is now expected to become Al-Nassr’s first signing of the summer transfer window. Reports indicate that the club reached an agreement with Real Mallorca for the Portuguese midfielder for a fee between $10.4 million and $22 million.



The deal had been held up because Al-Nassr could not formally register the player while the financial restrictions remained in place. With those restrictions now lifted, Costa’s transfer can finally be completed, and the midfielder can join the squad’s preparations for the new season.



Cristiano Ronaldo #7 and Samu Costa #24 during Portugal’s training session.



Al-Riyadiyah reported that the midfielder has already received the necessary approvals and is set to participate in Al-Nassr’s training sessions. Costa’s arrival would give the club an important new option in midfield after Marcelo Brozovic departed when his contract expired at the end of last season.



The 25-year-old Portuguese midfielder therefore arrives at a particularly important moment. Al-Nassr needs to maintain the quality of its midfield while simultaneously managing a squad built around one of football’s biggest stars.



And for Ronaldo, the development provides another reason for optimism. With the $280 million financial hurdle apparently cleared and Costa edging closer, Al-Nassr can finally concentrate on building the squad it needs for another season of domestic and continental ambitions.

items.title: Ronald Araujo joins Liverpool on loan from Barcelona: What are the terms of the contract?
items.description:
Ronald Araujo will be part of Liverpool next season, after arriving on loan from Barcelona. 
Ronald Araujo has joined Liverpool on loan from Barcelona for the 2026-27 season, with a verbal agreement between the two clubs reached on Friday and approved by Barcelona sporting director Deco. The Uruguayan defender is set to undergo his medical on August 8 before the move is finalized.



The deal is structured as a season-long loan that includes an option, but not an obligation, for Liverpool to sign Araujo permanently at its conclusion. That setup allows the Reds to evaluate his fitness and form, which dipped following a 2024 injury setback, before committing to a longer-term deal, while also giving Barcelona breathing room on their salary cap to register the rest of their squad for the season.



Araujo‘s departure comes after he fell down Barcelona’s defensive pecking order despite being one of the club’s four captains. Eric Garcia, Gerard Martin, and Pau Cubarsi have established themselves as Hansi Flick’s preferred center-backs, while Jules Kounde remains first-choice at right-back.



The 27-year-old, who debuted for Barcelona in 2019 and has made 213 appearances with 14 goals, still holds a contract at the club through 2031 after renewing in January 2025.




🚨🚨💣 EXCLUSIVE: Liverpool agree loan deal to sign Ronald Araujo from Barcelona, HERE WE GO! 🇺🇾Verbal agreement club to club with Barça now approved by director Deco.New centre back for #LFC with a surprise bomba. pic.twitter.com/kK4GIifmff— Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) August 7, 2026




For Liverpool, the move addresses an urgent need at the back. The club lost Ibrahima Konate to Real Madrid on a free transfer, and head coach Andoni Iraola has been dealing with injuries to Joe Gomez, Giovanni Leoni and Jeremy Jacquet, prompting him to request defensive reinforcements before the transfer window closes.


        


Barcelona looking to reinforce defense after Araujo’s exit



Araujo’s departure could coincide with Barcelona strengthening the very position that pushed him down the pecking order in the first place. The club is reportedly closing in on a two-year deal for Joao Cancelo, who would arrive from Al-Hilal for around €10 million.



Should the move go through, Flick would have two established options at right-back between Cancelo and Kounde, further reducing the need for Araujo as defensive cover on that side and reinforcing the logic behind sending him out on loan.

items.title: Arsenal snubbed by Tottenham as Cristian Romero reportedly closes in on Atletico Madrid move
items.description:
Tottenham rejected a move for Cristian Romero to Arsenal, while the Argentine reportedly closes in on a move to Atletico Madrid. 
Arsenal have been rebuffed in their approach for Cristian Romero, with Tottenham making clear they won’t do business with their London rivals as the Argentine defender edges closer to a move to Atletico Madrid.



The reigning Premier League champions turned to Romero after William Saliba suffered a serious back injury during France’s World Cup campaign, leaving Mikel Arteta’s side short at the back with the transfer window nearing its close. Arsenal had already seen an earlier approach for Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa rejected before shifting their attention to the Tottenham captain.



Spurs, however, wasted no time shutting the door. Fabrizio Romano reported that Arsenal made inquiries this week but that Spurs prefer to sell abroad, while a separate report from The Athletic stated that Tottenham’s hierarchy have categorically ruled out selling Romero to Arsenal under any circumstances.



That stance has left the door wide open for Atletico Madrid, who have emerged as the clear favorites for Romero’s signature. The Spanish club has already opened formal negotiations with Tottenham, seen an initial bid rejected, and is preparing a new offer, with Romano placing Atletico Madrid well ahead of Inter Milan in the race for the Argentine.



Cristian Romero of Tottenham. (Getty Images)



Inter, meanwhile, had reached a €40 million agreement with Tottenham but saw the move stall after failing to sell Benjamin Pavard to fund it and after Romero himself held off on agreeing personal terms — with reports suggesting the defender has a clause favoring a move to one of Spain’s traditional “big three” clubs.


        


Romero hinted earlier at a LaLiga move



Romero’s links to a Spanish move aren’t new. Speaking to Los Edul a few months ago, the defender admitted that a switch to LaLiga was something he’d long considered. “Growth is always on my mind, going to new places to keep growing. Playing in LaLiga is something I’m missing out on. I would love that, honestly,” he said at the time.



Those comments now look particularly timely given how close he appears to Atletico Madrid. While Romero has been consistently linked with a move to Spain over the past year, his own words suggest the interest runs both ways.

items.title: Lionel Scaloni is Argentina’s ‘Plan A, B, and C’ ahead of the 2030 World Cup, says AFA president
items.description:
Argentina FA president admitted that Lionel Scaloni is the national team's "Plan A, B, and C" ahead of the 2030 World Cup planifications. 
Lionel Scaloni has served as the architect of Argentina‘s golden era, but with his contract set to expire at the end of the year, questions surrounding his future have naturally surfaced. As initial planning begins for the 2030 World Cup cycle, Scaloni remains “Plan A, B, and C” for Argentina Football Association (AFA) president Claudio Tapia.



Following a heartbreaking loss in the 2026 World Cup final, Scaloni cast doubt on his continuation during an emotional press conference that he was forced to cut short after breaking down in tears. A broader roster overhaul looms for the Albiceleste, which featured one of the oldest squads in the tournament, and the AFA remains determined to have Scaloni direct that transition.



In an interview with TyC Sports, Tapia expressed his unwavering desire for Scaloni to spearhead the next cycle: “Without a doubt, I want him to stay, we all want him to stay. We have spoken, and he has even expressed it himself as well, that the conversations were very advanced. I am a grateful guy, and that’s why I think we have to let him meditate, make the right decision, and we have to respect it.“



Tapia emphasized that he would give the manager full autonomy to evaluate his future without added pressure. “I can’t keep the ‘Gringo’ (Scaloni) chained up if he feels he doesn’t have the desire or doesn’t have a better projection. I want him to be well, and we should all want the same, even if it hurts us,” Tapia added.



Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni hugs AFA president Claudio Tapia after winning the 2024 Copa America. (Maddie Meyer/Getty Images)



With Scaloni’s contract expiring in December 2026, the AFA is eager to secure the manager’s long-term future. However, when pressed on whether the federation had prepared a backup option in the event of his departure, Tapia delivered a direct answer: “No, my Plan A, B, and C is Scaloni.“


        


Since his debut against Guatemala in 2018, Scaloni has compiled an extraordinary resume, amassing over 75 wins and just nine defeats while capturing two Copa America titles, a Finalissima, and the 2022 World Cup. As the federation sets its sights on the 2028 Copa America and the 2030 World Cup, executives remain convinced that Scaloni is the sole candidate for the position.



Family support could play key role in Scaloni’s decision



Scaloni’s emotional post-match remarks underscored the immense burden of leading the national team, noting that a full reset requires “building a group like this all over again… which will be hard to ever replicate. And it hurts me to my very soul.” However, the national team may have a crucial factor working in its favor to sway his decision.



According to TyC Sports journalist Rodolfo Cingolani, who conducted the interview with Tapia, he was told in an off-the-record conversation that Scaloni’s wife strongly supports his continuation at the helm. Based in Mallorca, Spain, with their family, Elisa Montero reportedly encourages him to remain in the position, believing the joy the Albiceleste brings him, paired with his trusted coaching staff, makes staying on the bench the right path forward.

items.description: A crop of young players emerges every season in the Premier League. items.description: Federation leaders are massing forces at the gates, but years after the first proposed selling off of its commercial legacy and the Qatar World CupIn recent decades the city of Salé, just across the river from Rabat on Morocco’s Atlantic coast, has undergone a remarkable transformation. At the start of this century it was a gritty working-class area, whose old town was still weathered enough to serve as a body double for the Somali capital Mogadishu in the film Black Hawk Down. But in recent decades, under the country’s autocratic government, the area has been transformed beyond measure, and largely beyond control.The population has trebled in the space of 40 years. Slums have been cleared, often forcibly, to make way for grand megaprojects: a new tram system, luxury tourist spaces, a sparkling marina, a blue-chip business park called Technopolis, and – since last July – the African headquarters of Fifa. And in a way, this hub of disruption and avarice, unshakeable volition and rampant capitalism, feels like the perfect location from which a besieged warlord might choose to make his desperate last stand. His signature chip wasn’t instantly eponymous. A search of the British newspaper archives shows that it was barely mentioned until Francesco Totti dusted it off for the internet generation at Euro 2000.It was at least another decade before Panenka was commonly used as a noun, and it did not have its own Wikipedia page until 2014, but in 2026 every football fan has an idea of what it means. items.title: New faces, gulfs in class and flawed drama: how 48 teams changed the World Cup
items.description: The first 48-team World Cup had its positives and negatives – do we need to brace for a 64-team future?It was less than 12 months after Gianni Infantino succeeded Sepp Blatter as president that Fifa announced the expansion of the men’s World Cup from 32 to 48 teams. The reaction was mixed. Diego Maradona said he was “delighted by Gianni’s initiative” because it allowed each country to dream of reaching the tournament, renewing their passion for football. Joachim Löw, then in charge of the world champions Germany, said: “I don’t think it’s a good idea to dilute the sporting value … In the long term, the quality suffers.”On the evidence of the first 48-team edition, won by Spain after 104 games across five-and-a-half weeks in North America, it’s fair to conclude Maradona and Löw both had a point. Continue reading...

items.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individualsWhat makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature. My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career.After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn.
